key_insight: AtomicRL improves long-horizon robotic manipulation by aligning reinforcement learning credit assignment and exploration with atomic subtasks.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a way to post-train vision-language-action policies for multistep manipulation and transfer simulation-trained improvements to physical robots.
method: Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization gates failed-subtask TD residuals at task boundaries while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping.
Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration adjusts task sampling and local exploration incentives according to subtask mastery.
A Real2Sim2Real pipeline connects online reinforcement learning in simulation with real-world deployment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports absolute gains over PPO of 3.6 and 4.0 percentage points on LIBERO-LONG across two VLA architectures, up to 9.5 points on CALVIN ABC-D, and an average 21.3% real-world improvement with Real2Sim2Real.
watch_item: Practical deployment depends on identifying reliable atomic task boundaries and mastery signals; the abstract does not quantify this implementation burden.
paper_title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
